words.definition: a quick look at something
words.example: I caught a glimpse of a deer running into the woods.
examples: Through the train window she caught a glimpse of the ocean.
He got only a quick glimpse of the comet before clouds rolled in.

words.definition: from a time long ago, before people wrote things down
words.example: Dinosaurs lived in prehistoric times.
examples: The museum displayed bones from a prehistoric sea creature.
Prehistoric people painted animals on the walls of caves.

words.definition: from far away
words.example: Scientists can control the robot remotely from a computer.
examples: The pilot flew the drone remotely from a tent miles away.
Engineers shut down the machine remotely when it overheated.

words.definition: the very top of a mountain
words.example: The climbers cheered when they reached the summit.
examples: A thick cloud hid the summit of the tall peak.
From the summit they could see three different valleys.

words.definition: to grow well and be healthy
words.example: Plants thrive when they get enough sunlight and water.
examples: Fish thrive in the clean, cool water of the mountain lake.
Children thrive when they feel safe and loved.

words.definition: very important; needed
words.example: Water is vital for all living things.
examples: Sleep is a vital part of staying healthy.
Clean air is vital for the survival of the forest animals.

words.definition: able to go under water
words.example: The submersible vehicle dove deep into the ocean.
examples: The submersible robot photographed fish far below the surface.
A submersible camera let the team film the shipwreck.

words.definition: a long, narrow, deep ditch in the ground or ocean floor
words.example: The Mariana Trench is the deepest trench in the ocean.
examples: Workers dug a trench to lay the water pipe.
Strange creatures glow in the dark waters of the deep trench.

words.definition: able to work or move by itself without help
words.example: An autonomous robot can clean the floor on its own.
examples: The autonomous car stopped at the red light by itself.
An autonomous submarine mapped the seafloor without a driver.

words.definition: when two things crash into each other
words.example: The collision between the two cars made a loud bang.
examples: A collision of two stars released a burst of light.
The referee stopped the game after the collision between players.

words.definition: the center or middle of something
words.example: The core of the Earth is very hot.
examples: The core of the apple held all of its seeds.
Honesty is at the core of true friendship.

words.definition: many different kinds
words.example: The rainforest has a diverse group of animals.
examples: Our class is diverse, with students from many countries.
A diverse diet includes fruits, grains, and vegetables.

words.definition: lasting forever
words.example: The friends made an eternal promise to stay close.
examples: The stars seemed like eternal lights in the night sky.
She believed in the eternal value of kindness.

words.definition: not doing anything; not active
words.example: The machine sat idle when nobody was using it.
examples: The boats lay idle at the dock during the storm.
He felt restless after an idle afternoon with nothing to do.

words.definition: very interesting; making you want to know more
words.example: The mystery book had an intriguing first chapter.
examples: The scientist shared an intriguing fact about glowing fish.
An intriguing clue led the detective to the hidden room.

words.definition: coming from living things; grown without chemicals
words.example: We bought organic apples at the farmer's market.
examples: The garden used organic soil instead of chemical sprays.
Organic farms try to protect the health of the land.

words.definition: to understand something fully
words.example: I can't fathom how the magician did that trick.
examples: Scientists still cannot fully fathom how deep-sea life survives.
She could not fathom why the door had been left open.

words.definition: very strong anger
words.example: The villagers feared the wrath of the storm.
examples: The king's wrath frightened everyone in the hall.
Sailors told stories about the wrath of the sea.

words.definition: a deep crack or opening in the earth
words.example: We looked down into the wide chasm in the rocks.
examples: A narrow bridge crossed the deep chasm.
The earthquake opened a chasm across the field.

words.definition: to slowly wear away
words.example: Waves can erode the rocks along the beach.
examples: Wind and rain slowly eroded the old stone steps.
Rivers erode the land and carve out canyons over time.

words.definition: to shine softly with reflected light
words.example: Dewdrops glisten on the grass in the morning.
examples: The wet stones glisten in the afternoon sun.
Tears began to glisten in her eyes.

words.definition: to break suddenly into many pieces
words.example: The glass fell and shattered on the floor.
examples: The loud thunder seemed to shatter the quiet night.
One small crack can shatter a whole window.

words.definition: stuck firmly inside something
words.example: The fossil was embedded in the rock.
examples: A sharp stone was embedded in the bottom of his shoe.
The memory stayed embedded in her mind for years.

words.definition: a person who stands guard and keeps watch
words.example: A sentry stood at the gate of the castle.
examples: The sentry marched back and forth in front of the wall.
Like a sentry, the lighthouse watched over the rocky coast.
